name: Project Status Report
one_liner: The regular one-page dashboard of where the project stands, for the PSC.
purpose: Produced by the Project Manager (PM) and regularly submitted to the Project Steering Committee (PSC) and other stakeholders as per the Communications Management Plan. It provides a summary of the project's performance rather than detailed task-level information, covering costs, scheduling, scope/changes, risks and issues. It reports the status of important milestones for the current reporting period and provides forecasts for future reporting periods.
created_in: Executing Phase (Project Reporting, §7.4) — repeated every reporting cycle
approved_by: Project Owner (PO) is Accountable; the report is submitted to the Project Steering Committee (PSC)

traps: It is a summary for the PSC, not task-level detail — no task lists, no WBS lines.
Status Report is frequent (1–2 months) and one page; Project Progress Report is fuller and periodic/yearly.
The Quality Review Report is a third report: PM produces it from the Quality Review Checklist.
PO is Accountable for Project Reporting; PM is Responsible. PSC is only Informed.
The Contractor Status Report is written by the contractor; the PM summarises it inside this report.
